iterations.strategy: CORRECTNESS FIX (Category A). Root cause: iter_1 used std::vector<bool> tl_has(nthreads) as the per-thread 'has_any' sentinel. std::vector<bool> is the bit-packed specialization in C++: threads writing tl_has[tid] for adjacent tids share a byte in the underlying storage, and concurrent non-atomic writes corrupt each other's bits non-deterministically. As a result, some threads' has_any flag would read false during reduction even though those threads processed qualifying titles, dropping their per-thread MIN contributions. This is why iter_0 and iter_1 produced DIFFERENT wrong results despite identical source (e.g. iter_1 missed title id=1640975 '3:10 to Yuma' (2007, kind=movie), which has matching keywords {violence, fight}, cc subj=1/stat=4, mi rating='7.8', and 7 chn-matching ci rows — it must contribute to MIN(t.title) but its thread's flag got clobbered). Fix: replace std::vector<bool> with std::vector<char> (or std::vector<uint8_t>) for the per-thread has_any flag so each element occupies its own byte and concurrent writes to different indices are race-free. Keep the rest of the logic identical: same dim builds, same probe order (mk -> cc -> mi -> ci), same per-title cand_chn/cand_mi/cand_n tracking, same string MIN reduction across threads. The chn bitset build can remain parallel with OMP atomic |= on the uint64_t word (vector<uint64_t> stores 8 bytes per element, no false-sharing of bits across elements, and OMP atomic update on |= is well-defined for integer types); alternatively make it single-threaded — it touches only ~3.14M short strings and is cheap. No performance regression expected; only the broken thread-local sentinel is replaced.
